sector_center_basis: Nominal compass bearing of the published south-southwest description; approximate, not a surveyed lamp azimuth
bearing_convention: Clockwise from north, viewed from above
source_location: Results: Light pollution alters orientation behavior; Figure 3A
source_note: The paper's 210-degree statistic is the beetles' mean heading, not a measured lamp bearing. The previous 225-degree analysis centre represented southwest.
caption: Artificial light shifts dung beetle orientation at multiple levels. (a) Each of ten beetles repeatedly exits the arena, with ten trials per lighting condition; four light-on bearings are missing. The arena drawing is schematic. (b) Curves show kernel density estimates of the posterior population mean direction, with a common radial density scale; dots show each beetle's observed circular mean bearing. Bearings increase clockwise from north, viewed from above. The lamp icon is schematic. The arc is centred at 202.5° with a 45° half-width, using the nominal south-southwest bearing reported by Foster et al. (2021), rather than a surveyed azimuth. Sector probabilities and intervals are conditional on this approximate centre. (c) Population-level within-individual concentration, converted to mean resultant length using I₁(κ)/I₀(κ). (d) Between-individual concentration: the resultant length of the ten fitted individual mean directions, calculated in each draw. (e) Probability of an exit within the marked sector, using population direction and concentration (individual offsets set to zero); the dashed line marks the uniform expectation of 0.25. (f) The paired draw-wise difference in this probability, on minus off. Points show posterior means and bars show 89% highest-density intervals.
